text_blocks.snippet: Chronic lower back pain can be managed through a combination of approaches, including exercise, physical therapy, medication, and complementary therapies. Staying active, adopting healthy habits, and considering therapies like acupuncture or spinal manipulation can all play a role in reducing pain and improving function.
snippet_highlighted_words: exercise, physical therapy, medication, and complementary therapies

list.title: Staying active is crucial:
list.snippet: It's important to stay as active as possible, even with back pain. Follow your provider's recommendations for activity levels.

list.title: Strengthening and stretching:
list.snippet: Exercises that strengthen back and abdominal muscles, as well as gentle exercises like walking, swimming, or yoga, can be beneficial.

list.title: Physical therapy:
list.snippet: Physical therapists can guide you through specific exercises and stretches to improve mobility, reduce pain, and increase overall spinal function.

list.title: Over-the-counter pain relievers:
list.snippet: Acetaminophen (like Tylenol) and NSAIDs (like ibuprofen) are often the first line of treatment.

list.title: Prescription medications:
list.snippet: Tramadol, opioids, or other medications may be considered if over-the-counter options aren't sufficient.

list.title: Epidural steroid injections:
list.snippet: These can provide short-term pain relief by reducing inflammation around the spinal nerves.

list.title: Acupuncture:
list.snippet: Studies have shown that acupuncture can be effective in reducing pain and improving function for some people with chronic low back pain.

list.title: Spinal manipulation:
list.snippet: Chiropractors and osteopathic physicians may use spinal manipulation to relieve pain and improve spinal mobility.

list.title: Massage therapy:
list.snippet: Massage can help relax muscles and reduce pain.

list.title: Yoga and tai chi:
list.snippet: These practices can improve flexibility, strength, and balance, which can be helpful for managing back pain.

list.title: Cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT):
list.snippet: CBT can help individuals develop coping strategies for managing pain and improving overall well-being.
Heat and cold therapy: Applying heat or cold packs can help relieve pain and inflammation.
Back braces: These can provide support and stability for the lower back.
Weight loss: If overweight, losing weight can reduce the strain on the back.
Transcutaneous electrical nerve stimulation (TENS): TENS units deliver low-voltage electrical pulses to the skin to help reduce pain.
Radiofrequency ablation: This procedure uses heat to damage nerves that are sending pain signals, providing pain relief.
Implanted nerve stimulators: These devices send electrical impulses to nerves to block pain signals.
Surgery is rarely needed: Most people with chronic low back pain do not require surgery.

Seek professional guidance: It's important to consult with a healthcare professional, such as a doctor, physical therapist, or pain specialist, to determine the best treatment plan for your specific situation.
Lifestyle modifications: Adopting healthy habits, like regular exercise, good posture, and stress management techniques, can play a significant role in long-term pain management.
